  "id": "7adb9a0dec9a",
  "type": "tex",
  "title": "The per-section dual transport \\(\\mathtt{sliceDualTransport}\\)",
  "content": "Let \\(f : Y \\hookrightarrow X\\) be an open immersion of schemes and let\n  \\(M \\in \\Scheme.\\mathtt{Modules}\\,X\\). Write \\(\\alpha\\) for the open-immersion\n  structure-presheaf natural transformation with components\n  \\(\\alpha_U = (f.\\mathtt{appIso}\\,U).\\mathrm{inv}\\), a \\emph{\\(\\mathtt{CommRingCat}\\)}-level\n  ring isomorphism, and \\(\\beta = \\mathtt{whiskerRight}\\,\\alpha\\,\n  (\\mathtt{forget}_2\\,\\mathtt{CommRingCat}\\,\\mathtt{RingCat})\\) for its\n  \\(\\mathtt{RingCat}\\)-level shadow, with component\n  \\(\\beta_V \\colon \\mathcal{O}_Y(V) \\xrightarrow{\\sim} \\mathcal{O}_X(fV)\\)\n  (\\(fV := f.\\mathtt{opensFunctor}(V)\\)). Then for every open \\(V \\subseteq Y\\) there is an\n  \\(\\mathcal{O}_Y(V)\\)-linear isomorphism\n  \\[\n    \\bigl((\\mathtt{pushforward}\\,\\beta).\\mathtt{obj}\\,(\\mathtt{dual}\\,M.\\mathtt{val})\\bigr)(V)\n      \\;\\xrightarrow{\\ \\sim\\ }\\;\n    \\bigl(\\mathtt{dual}\\,((\\mathtt{pushforward}\\,\\beta).\\mathtt{obj}\\,M.\\mathtt{val})\\bigr)(V),\n  \\]\n  realised as a single \\(\\mathtt{LinearEquiv.toModuleIso}\\) that packages \\emph{both} leg (A)\n  --- the slice-Hom base-change reindexing across \\(f.\\mathtt{opensFunctor}\\) --- and leg (B)\n  --- the unit codomain ring-iso swap.   "id": "53577421ca15",
  "type": "tex",
  "title": "Gluing a sheaf of modules along an open cover",
  "content": "Let \\(D\\) be a glue datum of schemes (\\cref{def:gr_the_glue_data}), with index set \\(J\\), charts \\(U_i\\),\n  pairwise overlaps \\(V_{ij}\\), open immersions\n  \\(f_{ij} : V_{ij} \\hookrightarrow U_i\\), and transition isomorphisms\n  \\(t_{ij} : V_{ij} \\xrightarrow{\\sim} V_{ji}\\) satisfying the glue datum's\n  cocycle conditions; write \\(X\\) for the glued scheme and\n  \\(\\iota_i : U_i \\hookrightarrow X\\) for the canonical open immersions of the\n  charts. Suppose given:\n  \\begin{itemize}\n    \\item for each \\(i \\in J\\), a sheaf of \\(\\mathcal{O}_{U_i}\\)-modules \\(\\mathcal{M}_i\\) on the chart \\(U_i\\);\n    \\item for each pair \\((i,j)\\), a \\emph{transition isomorphism} of sheaves of\n      modules on the overlap \\(V_{ij}\\),\n      \\[\n        g_{ij} \\;:\\; f_{ij}^{*}\\,\\mathcal{M}_i\n          \\;\\xrightarrow{\\ \\sim\\ }\\;\n        (t_{ij} \\circ f_{ji})^{*}\\,\\mathcal{M}_j,\n      \\]\n      comparing the two charts' sheaves after restriction (pullback) to the\n      common overlap \\(V_{ij}\\);\n  \\end{itemize}\n  \\emph{subject to the following module cocycle conditions}, compatible with the\n  scheme-level cocycle of \\(D\\) (its triple transition data \\(t_{ij}\\) and the\n  overlap immersions \\(f_{ij}\\)), which are required as hypotheses on the family\n  \\((g_{ij})\\):\n  \\begin{enumerate}\n    \\item[(C1)] \\emph{self-identity:} the self-transition is the identity,\n      \\(g_{ii} = \\mathrm{id}\\) on \\(f_{ii}^{*}\\mathcal{M}_i\\) (with\n      \\(V_{ii}\\) and \\(t_{ii}\\) the diagonal data of \\(D\\));\n    \\item[(C2)] \\emph{triple-overlap multiplicativity:} over each common triple\n      overlap \\(V_{ijk} = V_{ij} \\times_{U_i} V_{ik}\\) the base-change transports\n      (\\cref{lem:modules_pullback_basechange_transport}) of the three transition\n      isomorphisms satisfy\n      \\[\n        \\widehat{g}_{jk}^{\\,i} \\circ \\widehat{g}_{ij}^{\\,k}\n          \\;=\\; \\widehat{g}_{ik}^{\\,j},\n      \\]\n      where \\(\\widehat{g}_{ij}^{\\,k}\\), \\(\\widehat{g}_{jk}^{\\,i}\\),\n      \\(\\widehat{g}_{ik}^{\\,j}\\) are the transports of \\(g_{ij}\\), \\(g_{jk}\\),\n      \\(g_{ik}\\) to \\(V_{ijk}\\) through the scheme-level triple transition\n      \\(t'_{ijk}\\) and its compatibility \\(t_{\\mathrm{fac}}\\), reassociated by the\n      pullback comparison \\cref{def:modules_pullbackComp} so that all three land on\n      the same sheaf -- the multiplicative, \\(\\mathrm{GL}_d\\)-valued cocycle\n      condition.\n  \\end{enumerate}\n  Conditions (C1) and (C2) are exactly the descent datum for the Zariski cover\n  \\(\\{\\iota_i\\}\\); it is subject to them that the gluing is well-defined. Out of this\n  data the construction produces a glued sheaf of \\(\\mathcal{O}_X\\)-modules\n  \\(\\mathcal{M}\\) on the glued scheme \\(X\\).\n\n  \\emph{Construction.} The category \\(\\ShMod(\\mathcal{O}_X)\\) of sheaves of\n  \\(\\mathcal{O}_X\\)-modules has all limits, and both pushforward along a morphism and\n  these limits preserve the sheaf condition; the glued sheaf \\(\\mathcal{M}\\) is therefore\n  built directly as a limit -- an \\emph{equalizer of pushforwards} -- rather than through a\n  hand-built presheaf of compatible families. Concretely, form the two parallel maps of\n  sheaves of \\(\\mathcal{O}_X\\)-modules\n  \\[\n    \\prod_{i} (\\iota_i)_{*}\\,\\mathcal{M}_i\n      \\;\\;\\underset{b}{\\overset{a}{\\rightrightarrows}}\\;\\;\n    \\prod_{i,j} (\\iota_i \\circ f_{ij})_{*}\\,\\bigl(f_{ij}^{*}\\mathcal{M}_i\\bigr),\n  \\]\n  where, on the \\((i,j)\\)-component, leg \\(a\\) pushes the \\(i\\)-th factor forward along the\n  overlap immersion \\(f_{ij}\\) using the unit of the pullback--pushforward adjunction\n  together with the pushforward-composition comparison\n  \\((\\iota_i)_{*} \\cong (\\iota_i \\circ f_{ij})_{*}\\circ f_{ij}^{*}\\) (the dual of\n  \\cref{def:modules_pullbackComp}), and leg \\(b\\) pushes the \\(j\\)-th factor forward and\n  additionally transports it across the inverse transition isomorphism \\((g_{ij})^{-1}\\)\n  and the glue datum's compatibility identity, so that both legs land on the common overlap\n  sheaf \\((\\iota_i \\circ f_{ij})_{*}(f_{ij}^{*}\\mathcal{M}_i)\\). The glued sheaf is the\n  equalizer\n  \\[\n    \\mathcal{M} \\;=\\; \\operatorname{eq}(a,b) \\;\\hookrightarrow\\; \\prod_{i} (\\iota_i)_{*}\\,\\mathcal{M}_i,\n  \\]\n  the sub-sheaf of tuples of pushed-forward chart sections whose two overlap restrictions\n  agree -- precisely the compatible families, now realised as a categorical limit rather than\n  a bespoke presheaf. The cocycle conditions (C1)/(C2) on the family \\((g_{ij})\\) are\n  \\emph{not} consumed in forming this equalizer object: the limit exists for any family of\n  transition maps. They are instead what make the equalizer descend correctly, and are\n  exactly the hypotheses pinned down downstream when the restriction isomorphisms\n  \\cref{def:gr_modules_glueRestrictionIso} are produced. This specialises effective descent\n  of sheaves of modules to the concrete open cover \\(\\{\\iota_i : U_i \\hookrightarrow X\\}\\)\n  supplied by a scheme glue datum, and is the form in which the Grassmannian's\n  tautological bundle and quotient are built.\n\n  The glued sheaf comes with three further structures, each recorded as its own block\n  downstream: the \\emph{restriction isomorphisms} \\(\\rho_i : \\iota_i^{*}\\mathcal{M}\n  \\xrightarrow{\\sim} \\mathcal{M}_i\\) compatible with the \\(g_{ij}\\) over the overlaps\n  \\cref{def:gr_modules_glueRestrictionIso}; the \\emph{characterisation up to unique\n  isomorphism} by the restriction property \\cref{lem:gr_modules_glue_unique}; and the\n  \\emph{descent of morphisms} -- a family \\(\\phi_i : \\mathcal{M}_i \\to \\mathcal{N}_i\\)\n  commuting with the transition isomorphisms glues to a unique \\(\\phi : \\mathcal{M} \\to\n  \\mathcal{N}\\) with \\(\\rho_i^{\\mathcal{N}} \\circ \\iota_i^{*}\\phi = \\phi_i \\circ\n  \\rho_i^{\\mathcal{M}}\\) \\cref{def:gr_modules_glueHom}.",

title: Quasi-coherent sheaves on an affine are sections-tilde
type: tex
updated: '2026-07-24T03:02:14'
---
\textit{Source: Stacks Project, Schemes, Tag 01HV, \texttt{lemma-spec-sheaves}.}
  Let \(X = \operatorname{Spec} R\) be an affine scheme and \(\mathcal{F}\) a quasi-coherent
  \(\mathcal{O}_X\)-module. Writing \(M = \Gamma(X, \mathcal{F})\) for its module of global sections,
  there is a natural isomorphism \(\mathcal{F} \cong \widetilde{M}\) of \(\mathcal{O}_X\)-modules,
  under which \(\Gamma(D(f), \mathcal{F}) = M_f\) for every \(f \in R\); in particular the sections of
  \(\mathcal{F}\) over a distinguished open \(D(f)\) are the away localisation \(M_f\). This is the
  affine quasi-coherent structure theorem (Tag 01HV, with the equivalence quasi-coherent-on-affine
  \(\simeq\) \(R\)-modules, Tag 01I8).

title: Triple-overlap bridges of the glue datum
type: tex
updated: '2026-07-26T00:08:22'
---
On the triple overlap \(V_{ijk} = V_{ij}\times_{U_i} V_{ik}\) the following three
  identities of morphisms hold, lining up the endpoints of the three base-change
  transports of the cocycle equation (C2):
  \begin{enumerate}
    \item \emph{(source)} the two projections of \(V_{ijk}\) to \(V_{ij}\) and \(V_{ik}\),
      followed by the overlap immersions \(f_{ij}\) and \(f_{ik}\) into \(U_i\),
      agree;
    \item \emph{(middle)} the \(ij\)-transport's target leg
      \((t_{ij}\circ f_{ji})\) and the \(jk\)-transport's source leg
      (through the cocycle transport \(t'_{ijk}\) and \(f_{jk}\)) agree as morphisms
      to \(U_j\);
    \item \emph{(target)} the composite \(jk\)-after-\(ij\) transport's target leg
      \((t_{jk}\circ f_{kj})\) and the \(ik\)-transport's target leg
      \((t_{ik}\circ f_{ki})\) agree as morphisms to \(U_k\).
  \end{enumerate}

title: Line bundle / Quot correspondence via the Abel map
type: tex

---
\textit{Source: [Kleiman], ``The Picard scheme'', \S 3,
  Thm.~3.7 + Def.~4.6 (cf.\ [Nitsure], ``Construction of Hilbert
  and Quot Schemes'', \S 1, where \(\Hilb_{X/S} = \Quot_{\mathcal{O}_X/X/S}\)).}
  Let \(C/k\) be a smooth proper geometrically integral curve. There is a
  natural transformation of presheaves on \((\Sch/k)^{op}\)
  \[
    A_{C/k} = \mathrm{abelMap} \;\colon\; \mathrm{Div}_{C/k}
      \;\longrightarrow\; \Pic^\sharp_{C/k}
  \]
  (\(\mathrm{Div}_{C/k}\) the relative-divisor functor of
  \cref{def:div_functor_carrier}, \(\Pic^\sharp_{C/k}\) the relative
  Picard functor of \cref{def:pic_sharp_carrier}), with the following
  \emph{defining property}: at a \(T\)-point represented by a family
  \(\langle \mathcal F, q\rangle\) (\cref{def:div_family}: a locally free
  rank-\(1\) quotient \(q \colon \mathcal F \twoheadrightarrow
  \mathcal L\) on \(C \times_k T\) with \(D := \ker q\) an invertible
  ideal sheaf, cutting out the relative effective divisor \(D \subseteq C
  \times_k T\)),
  \[
    A_{C/k}(T)\bigl(\langle \mathcal F, q\rangle\bigr)
      \;=\; -[\ker q] \;=\; [(\ker q)^{-1}]
      \;=\; \bigl[\mathcal{O}_{C \times_k T}(D)\bigr]
      \;\in\; \Pic^\sharp_{C/k}(T),
  \]
  the class of the associated invertible sheaf \(\mathcal{O}_{C \times_k
  T}(D)\), i.e.\ the additive inverse of the class of the ideal sheaf
  \(\ker q\) (Kleiman \S 3, Def.~dfn:Abel). This is the natural
  transformation in \(\mathrm{HasAbelMap}(C)\)
  (\cref{def:has_abel_map}), with witness
  \(\mathrm{abelMapWitness}(C)\) from
  \cref{def:inst_has_abel_map}.

For chart indices \(i, j \in J\) there is a natural isomorphism of functors
  \(\ShMod(\mathcal{O}_{U_j}) \to \ShMod(\mathcal{O}_{U_i})\),
  \[
    \beta_{ij} \;:\;
      \iota_i^{*}\,(\iota_j)_{*}
        \;\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }\;
      (f_{ij})_{*}\,(t_{ij} \circ f_{ji})^{*},
  \]
  identifying, for any sheaf \(\mathcal{N}\) on the chart \(U_j\), the restriction to
  the chart \(U_i\) of the pushforward \((\iota_j)_{*}\mathcal{N}\) with the
  pushforward along \(f_{ij}\) of the restriction of \(\mathcal{N}\) to the overlap
  \(V_{ij}\) along \(t_{ij} \circ f_{ji}\). Here the chart restriction \(\iota_i^{*}\)
  and the overlap restriction \((t_{ij} \circ f_{ji})^{*}\) are realised as the
  site-level restriction functors, isomorphic to the geometric pullbacks by
  \cref{lem:modules_restrictFunctorIsoPullback_mathlib}.
